title: What 11 days without sleep does to your brain 🧠
subject: sleep
description:
How long have you stayed awake? 👇

What happens to your brain if you don't sleep? In 1963, 17-year-old Randy Gardner stayed awake for about 264 hours while Stanford sleep researcher William Dement and a Navy doctor watched. By day 4 he saw fog around streetlights and mistook a street sign for a person; by day 7 his speech was slurred. Don't try this at home.

Sources: Ross, J.J., "Neurological Findings After Prolonged Sleep Deprivation", Archives of Neurology (1965); NPR ("Lessons from sleeplessness", 2024)

scenes.text: Stay awake 4 days, and street signs start looking human.
In 1963, a 17-year-old named Randy Gardner stayed awake for 11 days while scientists monitored him.
By day 4, he saw fog around streetlights and mistook a street sign for a person.
Then he decided he was a famous football player.
But here's the strange part. By day 7, his speech slurred, and by day 9, his vision blurred.
After 264 hours awake, he slept for 14 hours, and doctors found him healthy.
